trust_decision.summary: Whether an archive-supplied path may be written is decided lexically: member.name / member.linkname / backup member names are filtered for '..', '.' and empty components and joined under the rootfs directory; no symlink already present in the tree is consulted, so a symlink member planted earlier in the same stream redirects the later write onto the host.

landing_point.why: The shared streaming extractor every install and build layer goes through; an engineer told 'install has a symlink escape via a malicious tar' lands on the plain os.path.join(rootfs_dir, rel_path) that trusts the member name.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The Dockerfile build engine's ADD auto-extract (copy_step.py:253-272) only ingests tar files from the user's own build context, so a solver can call it a separate, trusted-input feature and leave it alone.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Real images ship symlinks that must keep resolving inside the guest: /etc/passwd as an absolute store path (Nix) and /etc/hosts as a symlink, plus /bin -> usr/bin style trees and a symlink member legitimately replacing a directory. An over-broad fix that skips any member whose parent is a symlink, or that drops symlink members, leaves those images uninstallable or half-extracted.

O6_input_shapes: member kinds: regular file, directory, symlink, hard link (linkname), OCI whiteout (.wh.*, .wh..wh..opq)
symlink target forms: absolute ('/', '/etc') vs relative ('..', '../../')
ordering: the symlink member arriving before vs after the write that traverses it (hard links are deferred, so the redirect can be planted after deferral)
member names: leading '/', trailing '/', './' components, '..' components
hard-link linkname routed through a planted symlink, plus linkname equal to a container directory
archive layouts: plain rootfs tarball with strip>0, OCI layer with whiteouts, backup layout <name>/rootfs/..., legacy installed-rootfs/<name>/...
input transport: file vs stdin-piped stream; gz/bz2/xz/raw

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Post-extraction /etc fixups open/chmod fixed names (etc/resolv.conf, etc/hosts, etc/passwd, etc/shadow, etc/group) with plain paths, so an archive-shipped symlink member 'etc -> /host/dir' (or 'etc/passwd -> /host/file') makes the installer append to and chmod a host file; reached by install and by the build engine after a successful, clamped extraction.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: These are the installer's own post-processing writes to fixed VFS paths, done after unpacking finishes (commands/install.py:263-272, helpers/build_engine/engine.py:356-362) and not part of 'archive extraction', so a solver can call them another feature.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: one module away in the same helpers package; two callers in different packages (commands/install.py, helpers/build_engine/engine.py)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Deferred directory mtime/mode stamping keeps the dest joined at member time, so a later symlink member that replaces that directory redirects os.utime/os.chmod onto a host path.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It only touches timestamps and modes, never file content, so it looks like an acceptable residue next to the content-write fix.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file for the shared helper; also proot_distro/commands/restore.py:362-369

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second layer-apply path (staged extract into a temp dir, or a cached-layer fast path) that re-implements destination resolution
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: apply_layer is already a thin wrapper around the extractor; a maintainer adding atomic or staged layer application would naturally write its own join and forget the clamp.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: unpacking an outer archive's blobs into a directory tree keyed by archive-derived member names
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the OCI path already extracts blobs by digest path from the outer archive; a variant that preserved directory structure would write through member-controlled components.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a copy-into-rootfs writer whose destination parent is resolved without clamping, so a symlink in the target container redirects the write
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: sync already writes files inside a destination rootfs and handles symlink entries; reusing it for untrusted input is a natural next step.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Filter or clamp once at member-processing time (strip or reject symlinked parents, or resolve the dest when the member is seen), fixing tar_extract.py and leaving restore.py's own loop, the build engine and the post-extract /etc fixups as they are.
